record.original_question: Is there an action φ on S1 which is induced by a topological action Φ, but is not induced by any smooth action Ψ on R2 preserving two transverse foliations?

evidence.quote: Question 6.2. Is there an action φ on S1 which is induced by a topological action Φ, but is not induced by any smooth action Ψ on R2 preserving two transverse foliations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathcal{F}_1$ and $\mathcal{F}_2$ be two transverse (one-dimensional) foliations of the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. The leaf spaces $L_i = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathcal{F}_i$ ($i=1,2$) are (in general non-Hausdorff) one-manifolds, and any homeomorphism (resp. diffeomorphism) of $\mathbb{R}^2$ that preserves both foliations descends to homeomorphisms of $L_1$ and $L_2$. By a standard construction one can compactify the data of these two leaf spaces into a circle $S^1$ (the "boundary circle" of the bifoliated plane), so that a homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^2$ preserving the two foliations induces a homeomorphism of this $S^1$.

Given a group $G$, say that an action $\varphi : G \to \mathrm{Homeo}(S^1)$ is induced by a topological action $\Phi : G \to \mathrm{Homeo}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ preserving two transverse foliations if $\Phi$ preserves a pair of transverse topological foliations on $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the resulting action on the associated boundary circle equals $\varphi$. Define analogously what it means for $\varphi$ to be induced by a smooth action $\Psi : G \to \mathrm{Diff}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ preserving two transverse smooth foliations.

Question. Does there exist a group $G$ and an action $\varphi : G \to \mathrm{Homeo}(S^1)$ such that $\varphi$ is induced by some topological action $\Phi$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ preserving two transverse foliations, but $\varphi$ is not induced by any smooth action $\Psi$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ preserving two transverse foliations?
